title: Analytical Literature Review: Saudi Arabia's Experience in Combating Violence, Extremism, and Terrorism
content: This analytical literature review examines Saudi Arabia's multifaceted approach to combating violence, extremism, and terrorism through analysis of diverse academic studies. The review explores five key dimensions of the Kingdom's counter-terrorism strategy: (1) security and law enforcement measures, including intelligence capabilities, border controls, and specialized counter-terrorism units; (2) innovative deradicalization and rehabilitation programs like the "Counseling and Care" initiative that provides psychological counseling, religious re-education, and vocational training; (3) counter-ideological efforts promoting moderate Islam through religious institutions, educational reform, and media campaigns; (4) international cooperation through participation in global coalitions and regional initiatives like the Islamic Military Counter Terrorism Coalition; and (5) socioeconomic development programs addressing underlying grievances that may contribute to extremism. Drawing on more than 30 studies, the review validates Saudi Arabia's comprehensive strategy while acknowledging ongoing challenges. The literature generally affirms the effectiveness of Saudi Arabia's efforts in mitigating terrorism within its borders and contributing to global counter-terrorism initiatives, though the author suggests future research should examine long-term impacts and the evolving nature of terrorist threats in the region.
